name: Marina and Harbour
description: The tiny rock-cut harbour where fishing boats are hauled up onto the ramp and pastel houses rise directly from the water. This is the most photographed corner of the village, busiest by far in daytime, with harbourside restaurants, the swimming rocks, and the start of the cliffside path toward Corniglia.
pros: Swimming off the rocks in summer

name: Via Discovolo (Upper Village)
tagline: The steep main street climbing to the vineyards
description: Manarola's single main street runs straight uphill from the harbour past guesthouses, wine shops, and the church of San Lorenzo, eventually giving way to the terraced vineyard slopes that produce Sciacchetra wine. Quieter than the harbour once you climb past the first few blocks, with genuine village character.
bestFor: Longer stays, wine lovers, quieter lodging

name: Volastra
tagline: A quiet hilltop hamlet above Manarola
description: A small hamlet perched in the vineyard terraces above Manarola, reachable by a shuttle bus, footpath, or the cliffside trail. Home to the Romanesque church of Nostra Signora della Salute and sweeping views over the coast, Volastra is where locals and wine producers actually live, far removed from the harbour crowds below.
bestFor: Escaping crowds, hiking bases, vineyard walks
pros: Best panoramic views of the coastline
cons: No real services beyond a bar or two
Requires a bus, hike, or drive to reach Manarola

name: Riomaggiore
description: The nearest of the five Cinque Terre villages, one train stop or a scenic cliffside walk from Manarola. Riomaggiore is somewhat larger with more guesthouses, shops, and a bit more going on after dark, making it a common alternative base for people who find Manarola too small or too quiet in the evenings.
bestFor: A change of scenery, more dining options, evening atmosphere
pros: More restaurants and shops than Manarola
cons: Just as crowded in peak season
Still no cars or coworking space
